evidence.detail: Rows ac1/label-and-compose-name (a container with the run's label, a network and a volume with the run's compose project name on the first context, a volume with the label, a container with the compose name and a volume with both on the second: each is an item owned by that run, on the context it was found on, present, adopted by the rule that proved it and ending on run finished; a second snapshot writes nothing), ac1/identity-recorded (the locator holds the Id of a container and a network, the CreatedAt of a volume and no Id, and each owner label carried; a labelled volume the engine shows without CreatedAt is a report and no item; the compose project name is derived from the label), ac1/protected (a volume the protect list covers by name and a container of a protected compose project, each with the run's label on it, get neither an item nor a report, and after every run finished neither was named to a stop or a remove and the volume holds its data). Green: proof/VELDO-0306/suite-green.txt.

The rows run the adapter against a real Ledger on a real control store, and send run finished through the real Signal, kind registry, probes, safety rules and removers; the project is in act mode by the owner's own signed command with a real key. The event stream is the output pipe of a real child process, waited on with the kernel's select and handed to the Service class's own docker_readable. Row integration/real-engine ran on this host against the real engine (context default, engine 29.2.1) with objects the row itself created under names made for that run: a labelled volume, network and container and an unlabelled volume were recorded from the real inspect records, a labelled volume created while the real event stream was read became an item from its event, the labelled ones were removed at run finished by the real client in the order container, network, volume, the unlabelled volume stayed as a report, and the row left none of its objects behind. Stand-ins: assumptions 1 to 3.

space306-read-one-context-only (the declared falsifier): ac1/label-and-compose-name red, the objects on the second context have no item. Beside it: space306-no-identity-still-an-item reds ac1/identity-recorded; space306-compose-project-not-in-the-locator reds ac1/protected. Each noop copy green.

assumptions: 1. THE ENGINE OF THE ROWS IS A STAND-IN, a class in the suite that holds containers, networks and volumes for two contexts and refuses as an engine does without a force option. Only integration/real-engine asks a real engine, and it runs only where the docker client answers on the context default or desktop-linux with an image there; in the gate's confinement it prints a SELFTEST SKIP line and adds no row, so the gate does not prove it. It ran green on the build host.

2. NOTHING SETS Service.space_docker YET. The service has no space ledger of its own, so no adapter is built for it in this repository: the pipes are in the poll set from the moment a later ticket sets the attribute. The loop of serve is not driven by a row; its select is read from its source (ac4/poll-set), and the rows call the Service class's own docker_pipes and docker_readable on a namespace that holds the adapter.

3. A RUN IS NOT GIVEN ITS LABEL YET. Putting the space label and the compose project name in a run's environment is the receiver's (design 6.3) and is not in this ticket's footprint; control_space_docker.given says what the two are. The rows label their objects themselves. Other stand-ins: the two checks of a switch to act (VELDO-0332, 0339), the process table (an empty fixture folder), the client that prints events (a real cat process).

4. THE FOOTPRINT GREW by control_space_signal.py and control_space_probe.py with their synced copies, for rule 1: it knew a Docker object by its engine Id alone, an engine gives a volume no Id, and so no volume could go at run finished. Rule 1 now passes a volume whose locator holds created_at when the engine shows a volume made at that time. Neither file is a protected path. The spec's History records it; it is the lead's to confirm.
5. IMAGES ARE NOT READ (VELDO-0328), and the adoption rule by compose's working folder and by bind source is VELDO-0307. An object those would give an owner is a report here.

6. A VOLUME'S IDENTITY IS ITS CreatedAt, which an engine gives to the second (the residual VELDO-0300 names): a volume removed and made again inside the same second under the same name is not told apart by it. Such a volume still has to carry the run's label or compose name to be the run's.

7. SEEN AND NOT CHANGED: control_space_probe.located takes "no such" in a client's words for the engine's answer that an object is absent. A real engine says "network <name> not found", so Signal defers a network removed by hand as not_in_ledger and never marks it gone (nothing is lost by that). The adapter reads the engine's own answer for each kind (absent).
rollback: Revert the change. Docker objects are neither recorded nor removed by Veldo.
